transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi… um, I guess I came because I’ve been scaring myself a bit. I keep having these thoughts like maybe it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And sometimes when I’m driving home, my mind goes to whether my family or even my students would be better off without me, which sounds awful saying out loud.

I’m a teacher, so I’m used to being the one holding things together—like, even when the copier breaks or a kid stays after class because they’re upset, you just keep going, don’t you? But then I get in the car afterward and it’s quiet, and those thoughts creep in. I don’t want to act on them… that’s why I’m here. It scared me enough that I thought I should tell someone.
How long have you been feeling this way? Have these thoughts been present most days, and do they last throughout the day?

It’s been… a while. About a year and seven months, I think. It started around when I took over the STEM assessment redesign at school, on top of my normal teaching load. I remember because everyone kept saying it was a “great opportunity,” and I was color-coding spreadsheets at my kitchen table until late, and my dining room basically became this depressing little office.

And then, sorry, I’m wandering—yes, that’s when it started. Since then it’s been there most days. Not always loudly the whole day, but it sort of hangs around, and by the time the school day ends and I’m driving home, it feels much harder to push away.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy, or found it hard to feel pleasure in activities, even when they used to make you happy?

Yeah… yes. That’s actually been one of the worst parts, I think.

I used to look forward to softball after school, and book club, and even just puttering around in my garden on weekends. I’d get kind of nerdy about tomatoes, like checking the little plant tags and pretending I knew what I was doing—my neighbor has this whole system with string and stakes, and I tried to copy it one year, but mine looked ridiculous.

But now I mostly either cancel or I show up and just… go through the motions. Same with robotics club. I used to really enjoy helping the kids get excited about it, but lately it feels like I’m just standing there saying the right things and waiting for it to be over. It’s not that those things are bad. They just don’t feel good anymore.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the contrary, feeling restless or unable to sit still?

I’m… not sure, actually. I haven’t really noticed one way or the other.

I mean, I know some days I probably look tired, but I don’t know if I’m actually moving slower or if I’m just… dragging myself through the day. With teaching, you’re kind of always moving—passing out worksheets, walking around the room, realizing someone’s borrowed all your pencils again and somehow none of them come back, which is its own mystery.

Sorry. Um. No, I don’t think I’ve noticed speaking slower or being unable to sit still in any obvious way. If it’s happening, I don’t think I’m very aware of it.

When you first started feeling this way, did you have a period where these symptoms were present every day for at least two weeks, and was there ever a time when you felt like you were starting to feel better before this came back again?

I think it really started around when I took over that STEM assessment redesign, on top of my regular teaching load. So… about a year and seven months ago now.

At first I kept telling myself it was just because I was busy, because everyone was busy, and the copier was always jammed and there were all these meetings with acronyms I swear people make up just to sound official. But looking back, it wasn’t just a rough week or two. It kind of settled in around then and didn’t really let up in any clean way.
Before this current period, did you ever have a time when you felt significantly better for at least a couple of months, where the symptoms completely went away or were much less severe?

Not really, no. I mean… I keep trying to think of a stretch where I was clearly back to myself, but it’s been kind of continuous since I took on that STEM assessment redesign on top of my normal teaching load.

That was about… a year and seven months ago now, I think. I remember because it was right when we were changing the curriculum maps, and everyone kept saying it would “streamline” things, which usually means it creates three new spreadsheets and a meeting that could’ve been an email.

But, sorry—no, I don’t think there was a couple-month period where it fully went away. It’s just been there since around then.
When you first started feeling this way, was there a specific two-week period where the symptoms were present nearly every day and clearly marked the beginning of this emotional state?

I don’t know if I can point to, like, a neat two-week block with a clear start date. It’s more that it began around when I took over the STEM assessment redesign along with my regular teaching load, and then it just… kept going.

That was about a year and seven months ago now. I remember because everything at school was suddenly rubrics and spreadsheets and “alignment meetings,” and somehow I was supposed to teach full-time and also make the whole thing make sense.

So, yes, that’s when this really started, but I don’t know that I could circle one exact two-week period on a calendar.
Have you felt this way continuously for the past two years, without a break of more than a few weeks at a time?

Not quite two years, no. It’s been about a year and seven months, I think—since I took over the STEM assessment redesign on top of my regular teaching load.

I remember it because that project sort of swallowed everything, and then there were all these extra forms and meetings, and I kept thinking, “Once this part is done, I’ll feel normal again,” but… it just kept stretching on. So, continuous, yes, but not for a full two years.
Have you had a low mood that has lasted for most of the day, more days than not, for the past two years?

Not for a full two years, no. It’s been… about a year and seven months, since I took over the STEM assessment redesign on top of my regular teaching load.

I keep measuring it by that, because that project sort of became the dividing line—before that and after that. And then it was just always there in the background while I was trying to keep up with everything. So, most days, yes, but not two years.
